notes:
Prospect summary and negotiation notes:
- Company: SparrowStack CX Cloud — mid-market SaaS (help desk + in-app assistance).
- Current stage: started on Hosted API POC, moving toward Dedicated because of predictable unit costs + VPC requirement.
- Primary workloads: real-time chat (support-agent), embeddings for semantic search, nightly reranking jobs.
- Targets: 75-100ms p95 chat latency (current hosted POC 120ms p95), steady-state throughput ~20-30 concurrent chat sessions, batch rerank jobs overnight.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — will trade some latency for cost but needs predictable monthly unit economics for forecasting.
- Technical reqs: VPC/private peering, SOC2 evidence, SSO via SAML, audit logs retained 12+ months, KMS integration for key management, EU data residency for subset of EU customers.
- Model & routing: primary model family open-weights (quantized) for embeddings and chat; want automatic fallback to smaller model when Dedicated capacity low; prefer routing by latency and cost tiers per route.
- POC notes: hosted POC provided token burn numbers; engineering wants Dedicated baseline sized at 2 x A100-equivalent for initial capacity with option to burst to 6 GPUs for campaign spikes.
- Pricing asks (prospect proposals):
  * 12-month committed plan, baseline 250M tokens/month, ramp schedule: 40% of commit in months 1-3, 70% months 4-6, 100% months 7-12 (Finance-driven request).
  * Burst pool: guarantee 50% additional capacity for short windows; ask for clear pricing for burst (prefer included minutes per month + overage rate).
  * Overage: capped per-token rate with monthly carry-forward of unused committed tokens (up to 2 months).
  * Ask for a mid-contract flexibility clause to change baseline by +/-20% once per year without heavy penalties.
- Redwood seller notes: initial proposal (v2) includes 12mo commit, 3-month ramp, burst runway as paid add-on, overage at 1.6x committed token rate, 30-day notice for baseline changes. Prospect pushing for lower overage (1.25x) and 2 months carry-forward.
- Quotes from call: "We need predictability — finance won't sign open consumption without a committed baseline." — Head of Finance.
- Security & legal: legal wants explicit language for EU residency scoping and proof of KMS integrations; security asked for SOC2 Type II report and an architecture whitepaper (attached in Drive).
- Open items: finalize explicit burst pricing, confirm ramp cadence acceptable to finance, agree overage multiplier and carry-forward rules, legal redlines for data residency.
- Risks: if overage cost too high, prospect may try hybrid self-hosting to shave unit economics. Also procurement timeline tied to end-of-Q2 budget cycles.
- Next steps (short): 1) Redwood to produce SOW with two pricing options (conservative/high utilization) by 2026-03-10; 2) Legal to exchange redlines (Sparrow legal) by 2026-03-17; 3) Finance alignment call week of 2026-03-22.
